Keep only the products that meet every stated need, using the rules.
- When the customer needs zero overdraft fees, drop any product with an overdraft fee above $0.00 (True Blue $25.00, World Blue $30.00).
- Drop any product whose monthly fee is above the customer's monthly fee budget (Beige $200.00, True Blue $75.00, World Blue $50.00).
- Drop any product whose minimum balance requirement is above the most the customer can keep (Lime Green $5,000; True Blue $25,000; World Blue $10,000; Beige $250,000).
- Drop a product whose fee-waiver threshold is above that balance ONLY when the customer wants the monthly fee waived or avoided (Lime Green $15,000; True Blue $50,000; World Blue $25,000; Beige $500,000). A waiver threshold is not a minimum balance requirement.
- When the customer wants cashback on general debit card spending (for example supplies, hardware stores, gas): Cobalt Blue's documents give 1.0% cashback on eligible debit card purchases. Hunter Green's 2.0% applies only at certified eco vendors, so it does not meet a general debit cashback need. Ask the customer whether debit cashback is a must-have. If it is, recommend only a product whose documents you read in kb_products show that cashback, because the recommended account must be ensured to meet every stated requirement. If it is only a nice-to-have, do not filter on it.
- Sky Blue needs a company within 4 years of formation, and its fee becomes $25.00 after the free period. Drop it when the company is older than that, or when the customer says a fee after the free period is not acceptable.
- If the customer wants an account better than their current one, ask whether their current account class should be left out, and leave it out only if they say so.
Example: zero overdraft fees, must-have general debit cashback, ATM rebates, and a fee waived on a balance of a few thousand dollars leaves only Cobalt Blue ($20.00 fee waived at a $2,500 daily balance, 1.0% debit cashback, up to $15 a month in ATM rebates).
